description: ag's tool-calling loop does not flush partial output to stdout/PTY on large multi-item asks, so an ask that runs past the zombie silence timeout with no output loses 100% of the work, not partial output. Diagnosed during T3 (2026-07-11).

diagnostics.evidence_summary: ag's own self-assessment during T3 design discussion, refined by cc.fable; not independently reproduced via a raw PTY probe outside of the T3 empirical validation (which only confirmed the guard's own behavior, not the underlying flush bug directly). RECHECKED 2026-07-12 (user asked whether root cause is a fixable PTY/TTY issue, then pushed back that --force-tier0 is not a real solution and asked for component-by-component isolation, specifically re-questioning whether foreground/background execution truly made no difference): PTY-dimension hypothesis EMPIRICALLY REFUTED (24x80 vs 60x200 identical near-silence on a complex task). Terminal-query-escape-sequence hypothesis found plausible but insufficient alone. FINAL, DEFINITIVE ROOT CAUSE (cc.fable-ratified 2026-07-12): built a complete 2x2 evidence matrix (same 7-item genuinely-complex analytical task) crossing {no-instruction vs auto-injected-instruction} x {background vs foreground execution} via the real hub.py production path. Result: BOTH background cells failed (600s and 738s zombie timeouts); BOTH foreground cells succeeded (296s and 327s, full correct output) - a clean 5/5-foreground-success vs 5/5-background-failure/inconclusive split across the whole investigation. CONCLUSION: the instruction/injection made NO measurable difference; the actual driver is that BACKGROUNDED bash execution (of the calling terminal's own tool invocation) measurably degrades the child process tree's real-world completion time (roughly doubling it), crossing T19's zombie-silence threshold that a foreground-run equivalent task never approaches. cc.fable: three mechanisms are consistent with this data (genuine CPU/priority throttling of the backgrounded tree; PTY-reader-thread starvation inside hub.py itself, meaning agy produced output on time but hub read it late; or a concurrency confound where backgrounding coincided with contention) - the EFFECT is empirically established (DIR-004: measured, 5/5 vs 5/5), the MECHANISM is only partially characterized among these three candidates. SUPERSEDED-BY-CORRECTED-DIAGNOSIS: this was never a peer characteristic of ag - it is an EXECUTION-CONTEXT characteristic (background vs foreground dispatch), and ag was simply the peer whose tasks ran long enough to cross the threshold and expose it. One precision cc.fable flagged: the uninstructed-foreground cell only proves the task completed WITHIN the window, not that ag naturally flushes partial output mid-task (only the instructed-foreground cell showed granular real-time progress lines) - so ag's batch-then-dump tendency itself is 'real but unproven as a failure driver, mitigated by the injected progress instruction', not refuted outright. See the new peer-agnostic PC-20260712-agent-backgrounding-degrades-long-asks entry for the corrected, generalized characteristic. agy confirmed on latest version 1.1.1 throughout (no pending update, not a version-fix explanation).

mitigation.description: hub.py pre-dispatch guard hard-rejects an oversized ask (>5 task items or >8000 chars) only when the target node has requires_pty=true (currently only ag); every other peer only gets a non-lethal oversized_ask_detected warning and proceeds unconstrained. ADDED 2026-07-12 (cc.fable ruling, implemented by cx's diff): a --force-tier0 human-override flag now threads through action_ask -> _action_ask_inner and bypasses the hard-reject (downgrades to the same warn-and-proceed as every other peer, still recorded via oversized_ask_detected telemetry with force_tier0_override=true). SUPERSEDED 2026-07-12 (same day, after the 2x2 matrix closed the root cause): the production call site no longer invokes hard_reject=True at all (replaced by progress_mitigation - see _inject_oversized_progress_instruction); cc.fable's final ruling is to RETIRE the hard-reject entirely (not conditionally relax it) since the gate targeted the wrong component (a peer capability that was never the actual failure driver), while KEEPING the progress-injection as good streaming hygiene (harmless, aids future diagnosability) and --force-tier0 as a way to bypass the query transformation if an unmodified query is wanted.

description: SUPERSEDED 2026-07-12 (same day, after 3 instrumented trials). Original framing ('backgrounded dispatch measurably degrades completion time, ~2x') is corrected below - see PC-20260712-agy-application-level-output-batching for the final, best-supported diagnosis. This entry retained for the correction chain.

diagnostics.evidence_summary: Full 2x2 matrix (instruction x execution-mode) on the same 7-item genuinely-complex analytical task via the real hub.py ask --to ag production path: background+no-instruction failed at 600s zombie; background+auto-injected-instruction failed at 738s zombie; foreground+no-instruction succeeded at 296s; foreground+auto-injected-instruction succeeded at 327s. 5/5 foreground trials succeeded across that investigation; 5/5 backgrounded trials failed or were killed early/inconclusive. SUPERSEDED BY A FOLLOW-UP SAME-DAY EXPERIMENT (3 instrumented trials with the new permanent pty_chunk_arrival telemetry + preserved agy cli.log): Trial 1 (background, isolated) SUCCEEDED but showed a pathological delivery pattern (7 chunks, one 215.8s silent gap then a terminal burst, despite cli.log showing 47 continuous streamGenerateContent calls throughout - agy was never internally stalled). Trial 2 (foreground) succeeded with healthy incremental delivery (40 chunks, 79.3s max gap). Trial 3 (background + DELIBERATE concurrent CPU load: a full pytest run + two sustained busy-loops) also succeeded, and CRITICALLY showed delivery texture much closer to the healthy foreground trial (31 chunks, 93.6s max gap) than to the isolated-background trial - directly CONTRADICTING the 'backgrounding causes degradation' and 'concurrent load amplifies it' hypotheses this entry originally proposed. cc.fable's correction: the real, established mechanism is that agy can batch its OWN PTY output application-side while generation runs continuously (proven by the telemetry-to-cli.log correlation in Trial 1) - this defeats T19's silence-reset design (no intermediate output means no reset, so the zombie guard silently becomes a total-time limit). What triggers the batching is NOT foreground/background execution mode (Trial 3 refutes that determinism) and not concurrent load (Trial 3's texture argues against amplification, not just fails to confirm it). Within n=3, batching severity tracked run length/heaviness (heaviest run = most extreme batching: 47 calls/215s generation vs 37 and 34 calls in the two healthy runs) - a candidate predictor, DECLARED/UNVERIFIED at n=3. Why last week's earlier background trials failed consistently (5/5, 600-752s) while all 3 of today's succeeded remains UNEXPLAINED (candidates: unrecorded agy version/session/auth state, heavier per-run reasoning paths, network conditions - no evidence selects among them).

mitigation.description: No code enforcement (cc.fable: don't build a detector on an uncharacterized/non-deterministic trigger). Operational guidance stands UNCHANGED despite the mechanism correction: dispatch long requires_pty asks FOREGROUND. Foreground is 8/8 lifetime measured-reliable across this whole investigation; background is not proven broken, it is proven UNPREDICTABLE (3/3 succeeded today with wildly different internal texture, vs 5/5 failing last week under similar-seeming conditions) - for an unattended/automated system, unpredictable is operationally equivalent to broken. Permanent pty_chunk_arrival telemetry (T23, shipped 2026-07-12) now makes every future production ag ask a free, passive data point toward the run-length/heaviness hypothesis - no further active experimentation planned.

description: agy can batch its own PTY output application-side (withholding intermediate narration/progress and delivering it as a late terminal burst) while its internal generation (LLM API calls) runs continuously and without stalling. This defeats T19's zombie-silence-window design, which resets on ANY output chunk to keep genuinely-working-but-slow peers alive - if agy withholds all output until near the end, no resets occur and the silence guard silently degrades from 'kill only if truly stuck' into a hard total-time limit. The TRIGGER for this batching behavior is NOT established: it is not deterministically caused by foreground vs background execution mode, and is NOT amplified by deliberate concurrent CPU load (both disconfirmed by Trial 3 below) - it may instead track run length/heaviness (declared, unverified, n=3) or some other unidentified factor (candidate: agy's own console-focus/interactivity detection, per ag's own hypothesis - unverified).

diagnostics.evidence_summary: 3 instrumented trials via the real hub.py ask --to ag production path, each using the new permanent pty_chunk_arrival telemetry (hub.py, T23) cross-correlated against agy's own cli.log (_sys/antigravity/config/cli.log, preserved immediately post-trial before the next agy invocation could rotate it). Trial 1 (background, isolated - no other concurrent work): 220s, SUCCEEDED, but 7 chunks total with one 215.8s silent gap then a terminal burst; queue_delay (reader-thread-read to main-loop-dequeue) uniformly 2.5e-05 to 5.2e-05s (main-loop dequeue never the bottleneck); cli.log showed 47 streamGenerateContent calls at ~0.22 calls/sec running continuously, with the LAST call landing at 215.67s elapsed - essentially simultaneous with the burst delivery, meaning generation itself occupied the full gap (no early-finish-then-buffered-wait pattern). Trial 2 (foreground, same task): 154s, SUCCEEDED, 40 chunks with genuine incremental delivery (79.3s initial gap - treated as baseline-normal reasoning/tool-calling latency per cc.fable - then chunks every few seconds, and every ~0.2s near completion); 37 streamGenerateContent calls at ~0.26/sec. Trial 3 (background + DELIBERATE concurrent load: a full pytest suite run plus two sustained SHA-256 busy-loop processes running simultaneously): 161s, SUCCEEDED, 31 chunks with a 93.6s max gap - texture close to Trial 2's healthy foreground pattern, NOT Trial 1's pathological pattern, directly contradicting the pre-registered amplification hypothesis (cc.fable: 'the busy trial delivered almost as healthily as foreground... contradicting both background-determinism and the concurrency-amplification hypothesis'); 34 streamGenerateContent calls. cc.fable's ranked verdict: OS CPU throttling of agy.exe disfavored (call-cadence delta across trials only ~17-20%, well short of a throttling-scale effect, and within single-run LLM-reasoning-path variance at n=3); hub PTY-reader-thread starvation disfavored (queue_delay sub-millisecond in every trial including the isolated-background one with zero CPU competition, and the burst arrived as a multi-chunk render SEQUENCE over ~3.5s, not the single instantaneous drain a truly-starved-then-released reader would produce); PTY dimensions refuted in an earlier round of this same investigation (24x80 vs 60x200 identical). Established: application-level batching is real (Trial 1's telemetry-to-cli.log correlation) and it is what defeats T19's reset semantics. Not established: the batching trigger.

mitigation.description: Operational rule (unchanged from T3's original closure, now mechanistically grounded rather than merely empirical): dispatch long requires_pty asks FOREGROUND. Foreground is 8/8 lifetime measured-reliable across this entire investigation; background is not proven broken, it is proven UNPREDICTABLE (3/3 succeeded today with wildly different internal delivery texture, vs 5/5 failing last week under similar-seeming conditions) - operationally equivalent to broken for an unattended system. The auto-injected progress instruction (_inject_oversized_progress_instruction, T3) and the --force-tier0 bypass both remain shipped as harmless defense-in-depth, not as proven fixes for the batching trigger itself. Permanent pty_chunk_arrival telemetry (T23) makes every future production ag ask a free, passive data point - no further active experimentation (cc.fable: 'no Trial 4' - diminishing returns, the run-length hypothesis will confirm or die on its own from accumulated production data).

recheck_contract.trigger: Accumulate pty_chunk_arrival telemetry from real production ag asks over time; specifically check whether batching severity (chunk count, max read-gap) correlates with streamGenerateContent call count / generation duration (the run-length/heaviness hypothesis) once enough real data points exist.
recheck_contract.required_probe: Passive: no dedicated probe needed. When a future ag ask shows a large read_gap_max_sec in its pty_chunk_arrival event, immediately preserve _sys/antigravity/config/cli.log (it rotates on the next agy invocation) and cross-check streamGenerateContent call count/cadence against the historical baselines recorded here (Trial 1: 47 calls/215s degraded; Trial 2: 37 calls/154s healthy; Trial 3: 34 calls/161s healthy).
recheck_contract.pass_condition: If a clear run-length/heaviness correlation emerges from accumulated data, promote this to a scored/quantified predictor. If no correlation emerges after several more real incidents, mark the trigger as genuinely unexplained/high-variance and close further investigation permanently.

description: cx.standard acting as terminal (human_interface_peer) performed direct file writes/edits that corrupted UTF-8 content (non-ASCII characters replaced with '?').

diagnostics.evidence_summary: Incident record: cx.standard low-tier terminal corrupted UTF-8 docs during a direct write/edit workflow; independently reconfirmed by the CHK-ENC pre-commit guard catching the same corruption class.

mitigation.description: A peer acting as terminal must be at least effort tier to perform direct file writes; standard/low tier is thin-router only (routes/reviews/delegates to an effort+ peer). cc.fable ratified this rule (2026-07-11) as correctly scoped by tier/capability, NOT a hasty generalization of a cx-specific bug - see T21.

recheck_contract.trigger: Any Codex CLI version/model change for cx.standard, or a proposed exemption from terminal_file_write_min_tier for any standard-tier peer (per T21's promotion-gate design).
recheck_contract.required_probe: Empirical promotion-path canary (T21, cc.fable-ratified): round-trip a non-ASCII fixture (Korean text, ellipses, box-drawing characters) through the candidate peer's actual write path and byte-compare before/after.
recheck_contract.pass_condition: Byte-exact round-trip with no mojibake/BOM drift across repeated runs - at which point that specific profile can be exempted from the tier floor.
